messages.author: 194004d81259bcfd
messages.subject: allele-specific vs total copy number
parts:
I noticed that aroma.affymetrix only gives total copy number
estimates, but not allele-specific copy numbers. Is it because allele-
specific copy numbers for Affy SNP 6.0 arrays are not reliable so
shouldn't be used?

Thanks!
Yu Chuan

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] allele-specific vs total copy number
parts:
Hi,

if you replace the argument combineAlleles=TRUE with
combineAlleles=FALSE the RmaCnPlm (or whatever *CnPlm you are using)
will fit an allele-specific model. It will provide you with (thetaA,
thetaB) estimates (instead of total theta estimates). Use
extractMatrix(ces)/extractDataFrame(ces), where ces <-
getChipEffectSet(plm), to extract the theta estimates.

Since none of the downstream methods/models (e.g.
FragmentLengthNormalization, GladModel, CbsModel, ...) supports
allele-specific estimates you are on your own after fitting the CnPlm.
I know that Adam Olshen is working on an allele-specific extension
for the CBS method.

There are no reports that allele-specific estimates from GWS6 should
be bad - to me that sounds unlikely and I don't see why it shouldn't
work.

Cheers

Henrik

On Wed, Jun 11, 2008 at 10:55 PM, Yu Tai <mbc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Thanks! So there is no method which can segment allele-specific copy
> numbers?

> Why can't current methods for segmenting total copy numbers be
> directly applied to allele-specific copy numbers?

>
> Does this mean whether or not I put combineAlleles=FALSE, it gives the same
> copy number estimate for a SNP on Affy 6.0?

No. With combineAlleles=FALSE the CnPlm estimates the *chip effects*
{(thetaA,thetaB)} and with combineAlleles=TRUE it estimates the total
chip effect {theta}. See our paper what "chip effect" means. Raw CNs
are then calculated as the log-ratio of chip effects between two
arrays.

/Henrik
